tools.name: search_images
tools.description: Find images for sale by description, mood, colour or subject — a plain description of the feeling or scene works as well as a keyword, so pass what the person actually said. Give target_width and target_height when the image is destined for a specific screen — results are then ranked by how close ea

tools.name: get_image
tools.description: Everything known about a single listing: its description, keywords, price in credits and money, the license it sells under, and a preview. Use after search_images when the person wants a closer look at one option.

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: The collections available in the store, with how many images are in each. Use for browsing when there is no particular search in mind; prefer search_images when the person has described what they want.

tools.name: get_licence
tools.description: The full terms an image is sold under: what the buyer may and may not do with it. Read this before recommending a purchase, and whenever the person asks what they are allowed to do with an image. "personal" (the default) is what credits and a card one-off buy; "commercial" is the business licence, s

tools.name: unlock_collection
tools.description: Open a PRIVATE collection to the signed-in buyer, using the address and access code its photographer gave them — for example a wedding or client gallery whose pictures are also for sale. Afterwards search_images, get_image and list_collections include it for this buyer, and its images can be bought

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The signed-in buyer: their credit balance, subscription status, how many images they already own, and whether a free trial is still available. Call this before proposing a purchase, so you know what they can already afford. Requires sign-in.

tools.name: start_trial
tools.description: Give the signed-in buyer 3 credits free, once per email address, ever, and never to an account that has paid here. Offer it when get_account says trial_available, someone wants an image, has no credits and has not tried the store before — AND the trial would buy that image: its price.credits is no m

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Return a payment link for the person to open in a browser: either a subscription plan, or a single image bought outright (only where price.card_available is true) — or that image's commercial license, with licence=commercial, where price.commercial is not null. The commercial license is sold only th

tools.name: fulfil_image
tools.description: Deliver an image to the signed-in buyer, spending the image's price in credits (price.credits in search_images and get_image — often 1, sometimes more) if they do not already own it. Credits buy the personal license only; the commercial license is bought with create_checkout, and this then delivers

tools.name: list_entitlements
tools.description: Everything the signed-in buyer has bought, newest first. Re-downloading any of them with fulfil_image costs nothing. Pass include_previews: true whenever the person wants to see their library: small pictures (at most 12 per page) without a fulfil_image per image. Requires sign-in.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_licence" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_checkout · Private data: unlock_collection, start_trial, create_checkout, fulfil_image · Public sink: start_trial.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_checkout · Private data: unlock_collection, start_trial, create_checkout, fulfil_image · Public sink: start_trial

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
